title: Introduce tenant-gpu-fanout module and iam-credential-rotator for private TF state decoupling
author: Dmitri Volkov
description:
Motivation: Private deployments currently keep GPU node pools, IAM roles, and TF state anchored to the same monolithic state file. This makes tenant onboarding, credential rotation, and network reassignments risky and slow. This PR introduces two opinionated Terraform modules (tenant-gpu-fanout and iam-credential-rotator), a light migration helper, and a documented rollout/rollback path to gradually decouple GPU pools and IAM credentials per-tenant while maintaining an auditable state migration path.

Summary of changes: added a new module terraform/modules/tenant-gpu-fanout that creates tenant-scoped GPU node subpools, tenant-local subnet attachments, and lease metadata outputs; added terraform/modules/iam-credential-rotator to manage short-lived IAM service account keys with optional KMS/HSM wrapping; introduced a migration helper script tools/tf-migrate-fanout (bash + minimal Go helper) that creates new per-tenant state shards and migrates resources with state-lock safety checks; updated top-level environments to consume the new modules via optional for_each maps to allow phased rollout; added unit/integration test harness for the modules under tests/terraform/tenant-fanout; and updated docs/terraform/private/gpu-fanout.md with rollout steps and rollback playbook.

Why this is different: existing TF work covers TF state shard boundaries and GPU allocation operators, but this PR focuses on a gradual fanout pattern (one tenant -> many small nodepools) plus an automated credential rotation primitive tailored for Private installations where KMS/HSM integration and air-gapped rollout are common requirements. It also ships a migration helper rather than an immediate state rewrite to reduce blast radius.

Implementation details: the tenant-gpu-fanout module exposes the following inputs (high-level): tenant_id, preferred_zones (list), gpu_profile, min/max_pool_size, node_taints, network_attachment (object), state_prefix. Outputs: list of nodepool ids, per-pool subnet ids, lease_metadata (string JSON), and state_shard_key. The module implements a provider aliasing pattern so each tenant's nodepool resources can be targeted to a different GCP/AWS project or account if the environment map is provided. The iam-credential-rotator module creates a short-lived service account key (rotated by TTL), an optional KMS-wrapped secret version, and a rotation trigger hook compatible with our private-installer webhook contract. Rotations produce a new secret path and increment the rotation_index output to enable consumers to do atomic config swap.

Migration strategy (high level): 1) Enable tenant-gpu-fanout in a single non-prod environment with for_each limited to a test-tenant map; 2) Run tools/tf-migrate-fanout --preview to validate state changes; 3) Apply in canary mode to migrate nodepool resources to per-tenant shards; 4) Switch private-installer to read lease_metadata outputs and create tenant leases from the new nodepools; 5) Once stable, run rotate mode for IAM credentials (iam-credential-rotator) and switch workload identities over to new key material. The migration helper includes pre-apply validation (state lock check, resource diff summary), a timed backoff loop for API rate errors, and an idempotent rollback marker in state to allow safe reversal.

Testing and CI: added three new Terraform integration scenarios (smoke, canary, and regression) that run in our existing CI but in a sandboxed AWS/GCP test account. CI initially failed on static analysis (terraform fmt) and the IAM policies lint; fixes were pushed and CI reran. New tests assert that nodepools created by fanout include expected taints, that network attachments maintain existing CIDR allocations, and that rotation creates a new wrapped secret and increments rotation_index.

Security considerations: rotation module defaults to short TTLs and requires explicit kms_key input for wrapping in Private installs. The module has an allowlist for principals that can request rotations and emits audit events via our audit-log exporter hook. The PR includes updated SLO/alert suggestions in the docs for increased IAM key churn.

Rollback plan: the migration helper writes a migration marker into the source state and creates a copy of the prior state under state-prefix/backup/<migration-id>. The rollback playbook (docs/.../gpu-fanout.md) provides commands to revert private-installer to the previous lease source and to re-run tf-migrate-fanout --rollback which re-anchors resources back into the original state file. We validated rollback in integration by migrating a canary tenant and then rolling back under simulated API latency.

Related: touches private-installer and private-helm charts (annotations to consume rotation webhooks), and the change is coordinated with ENG-4201 (tenant onboarding) and ENG-4132 (credential hardening).

Checklist: [x] module code + examples [x] migration helper + preview mode [x] docs + rollout/rollback playbook [x] CI integration tests [x] reviewer feedback addressed

Commits (high level): see commits list below for granular messages.

release_notes:
- Added tenant-gpu-fanout Terraform module to create per-tenant GPU nodepools and subnet attachments.
- Added iam-credential-rotator module for short-lived service account keys with optional KMS wrapping.
- Migration helper (tf-migrate-fanout) to preview/apply/rollback per-tenant state splits.
- Docs and rollback playbook for staged rollout.
notes: This change was intentionally staged: we prioritized a preview-first migration helper to avoid a single-shot state rewrite. Ops runbook entry updated; coordinate with platform-sre before enabling on production environments.
